Problem Statement:
Strip problematic private escape sequences

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix

- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

from rich.ansi import AnsiDecoder

def test_decode():
    console = Console(
        force_terminal=True, legacy_windows=False, color_system="truecolor"
    )
    console.begin_capture()
    console.print("Hello")
    console.print("[b]foo[/b]")
    console.print("[link http://example.org]bar")
    console.print("[#ff0000 on color(200)]red")
    console.print("[color(200) on #ff0000]red")

    decoder = AnsiDecoder()
    lines = list(decoder.decode(terminal_codes))

    expected = [

        Text("bar", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("link http://example.org"))]),
        Text("red", spans=[Span(0, 3, Style.parse("#ff0000 on color(200)"))]),

steps.message:
The issue is that private ANSI escape sequences (`\x1b0` through `\x1b?`) are not being stripped by the ANSI parser in `rich/ansi.py`, which can cause cursor movement and garbage output.

The current regex used for tokenizing ANSI sequences is:
```python
re_ansi = re.compile(
    r"""
(?:\x1b\](.*?)\x1b\\)|
(?:\x1b([(@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))
""",
    re.VERBOSE,
)
```
The second part of the regex `(?:\x1b([(@-Z\\-_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))` handles sequences starting with `\x1b` followed by a character in the range `@-Z` or `\-` or `_`, or a sequence starting with `\x1b[`.

Private escape sequences are `\x1b` followed by a character in the range `0-?` (ASCII 48-63). The current regex does not include these characters immediately following `\x1b` (unless they start with `[`).

To fix this, we need to add `0-?` to the character class that follows `\x1b`.

FILES: `rich/ansi.py`:11-13

ROOT CAUSE: The `re_ansi` regular expression does not match private escape sequences (starting with `\x1b` followed by `0-?`), allowing them to pass through to the output.

CHANGE: Update the character class in `re_ansi` from `[@-Z\\-_]` to `[0-?@-Z\\-_]` to include the problematic private escape sequences.

TEST: Create a new test case in `tests/test_ansi.py` that includes strings like `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` and verifies that `Text.from_ansi()` strips them.
